verdict.summary: Todoist OAuth is fully self-serve: register an app in the App Management Console (or register at runtime through dynamic client registration), request data:read or data:read_write, and any Todoist user can connect the same day with no review. The main things to get right are rotating refresh tokens, where replaying a used token revokes all of that user's tokens for your app, and building on API v1, because REST v2 now returns 'This endpoint is deprecated'.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: Create the app, set a redirect URL, implement the code exchange; no verification steps.

timeToProd.assumes: A standard OAuth app reading and writing tasks with data:read_write; listing in Todoist's integrations directory is optional and not needed for users to connect.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: The docs describe submission to the official integrations list as optional marketing; the Authorization section has no review step.

prerequisites.why: Apps are created in the App Management Console inside Todoist settings.

prerequisites.item: A redirect URL configured on the app
prerequisites.why: The OAuth flow redirects back to a configured URL; redirect_uri is optional in the authorize request.

prerequisites.item: An app name that isn't primarily 'Todoist' and a non-affiliation disclaimer
prerequisites.why: Brand rules require names like 'X for Todoist' and a description stating the app isn't affiliated with Todoist.

scopeTiers.impact: Can only create tasks; least-privilege option for capture agents.
Read (or read and modify) tasks, projects, labels and filters. data:read_write includes task:add and data:read. What most agents need.
Deleting tasks/labels/filters or projects, and listing backups without MFA. No review, but users see them on the consent screen, so request only if needed.

steps.title: Create the app
steps.detail: Open the App Management Console in Todoist settings, create an app (named like 'X for Todoist'), and copy the client ID and secret.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: Console URL returned HTTP 200 (login-gated SPA); we didn't sign in.

steps.title: Set the redirect URL and check refresh tokens are on
steps.detail: Add your OAuth redirect URL. New apps get refresh tokens by default; legacy apps can opt in, but the setting can't be turned off afterwards.

steps.title: Alternatively, register at runtime
steps.detail: Todoist supports RFC 7591 dynamic client registration at https://api.todoist.com/oauth/register (no auth, rate-limited per caller) and Client ID Metadata Documents with PKCE, useful for MCP-style clients.

evidence.label: tested
evidence.note: Metadata lists registration_endpoint and client_id_metadata_document_supported: true.

steps.title: Implement the authorization code flow
steps.detail: Redirect to https://app.todoist.com/oauth/authorize?client_id=...&scope=data:read_write&state=.... Exchange the code at POST https://api.todoist.com/oauth/access_token with client_id, client_secret and code. Check state.

steps.title: Implement rotating refresh
steps.detail: Access tokens expire after 3,600 s. On HTTP 401 with error_code 477, POST grant_type=refresh_token and store the new refresh token immediately; never reuse a consumed one after the 60-second grace window.

steps.title: Build on API v1 with sync limits in mind
steps.detail: Use /api/v1/ endpoints. Prefer incremental syncs and batch up to 100 commands per request (counts as one) to stay under 1,000 partial / 100 full syncs per user per 15 minutes.

steps.title: Test with your own account and ship
steps.detail: Authorize, run read/write flows, and launch; any Todoist user can connect.

steps.title: Optional: submit to the integrations directory
steps.detail: Submit for evaluation and inclusion in Todoist's official integrations list for marketing; not required for OAuth to work.

agentCanDo: Implement the OAuth code flow, state checks and rotating refresh
Register clients dynamically or via a Client ID Metadata Document
Build incremental sync and command batching under rate limits
Migrate any REST v2 / Sync v9 code to API v1
Write the app description with the non-affiliation disclaimer
humanMustDo: Sign in to Todoist and create the app in the App Management Console
Copy and store the client secret
Optionally submit the integration for directory listing

blockers.symptom: All of a user's tokens suddenly stop working and they must re-authorize
blockers.cause: A consumed refresh token was presented after the 60-second grace window; Todoist treats it as replay and revokes all the user's tokens for the app.
blockers.fix: Serialize refreshes per user and atomically persist the newest refresh token.
Refresh and retry with the new token; don't retry the same token.

blockers.symptom: Old endpoints return 'This endpoint is deprecated'
blockers.cause: REST API v2 and Sync v9 were retired in favour of the unified API v1 (/api/v1/), which also uses different IDs.
blockers.fix: Follow the 'Migrating from v9' guide and switch to /api/v1/ paths and IDs.

evidence.label: tested
evidence.note: GET https://api.todoist.com/rest/v2/tasks returned 'This endpoint is deprecated' pointing to /api/v1/ on 2026-10-20.

blockers.fix: Copy the client ID from the App Management Console, or re-register the dynamic client.

evidence.label: tested
evidence.note: Observed with a dummy client_id on 2026-10-20.

blockers.cause: Per-user caps of 1,000 partial and 100 full syncs per 15 minutes.
blockers.fix: Use incremental sync tokens, batch commands, and use webhooks instead of polling.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: The exact throttle error isn't quoted in the docs section we read.

nuances.text: Legacy apps created before refresh tokens became the default get effectively non-expiring tokens (expires_in 315360000, no refresh token). Opting a legacy app into refresh tokens is one-way and doesn't convert existing tokens.
Todoist hosts an official MCP server at https://ai.todoist.net/mcp that uses the same Todoist authorization server and requests data:read_write.
Public clients can use PKCE with token_endpoint_auth_method 'none'; confidential clients default to client_secret_post.
Webhook deliveries that fail are retried after 15 minutes, at most three times, so don't rely on webhooks alone for consistency.
Users can migrate a personal API token to an OAuth token via POST /api/v1/access_tokens/migrate_personal_token, which helps move existing PAT-based users onto OAuth.

tested: GET https://api.todoist.com/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server: registration endpoint, S256 PKCE, grants authorization_code/refresh_token, scopes task:add data:read data:read_write data:delete project:delete (and more), client_id_metadata_document_supported true
POST https://api.todoist.com/oauth/access_token with no body: 400 invalid_client 'Client credentials required'
GET https://api.todoist.com/rest/v2/tasks: 'This endpoint is deprecated' message pointing to /api/v1/
